newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil firms on both high and low sulphur.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil firms on both high and low sulphur.

text.p: High and low sulphur cracked fuel in NWE made late gains on Friday, bolstered by crude and sentiment that fuel should correct recent losses.
Thin trade on barges saw prices up at $111-112, $1-2 a tonne up on Thursday, but a good $2-3 up on early morning trade. Good ARA supply struggled to show higher prices, with demand limited.

The high sulphur cracked market was firmer around $104 fob NWE, fulfilling earlier hopes the spread, against a relatively strong Med, would narrow. Russian straight run material appeared less threatening to the cracked market. An M-100 was understood sold at two means +$2.50-$3.00.
Low sulphur cracked barges were stronger on the back of higher paper levels and late swaps numbers also pushed cargoes.
December paper traded at $125 lifting physical cargoes comfortably above $120 fob NWE. But, it was uncertain whether the mini-rally would hold over the weekend unless wet demand kicks in.

"There's late November interest, but I also see some good offers," said one trader. Some traders felt recent deals could kick-start prices higher. A cargo traded yesterday at $121.50 fob NWE traded again on Friday at high cif Med +$3 basis two Italian ports. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8980
